sentences.text: Angustinaripterus was a basal pterosaur belonging to the family Rhamphorhynchidae, found in Dashanpu near Zigong in Sichuan province, China.
Its skull is very elongated and flat in shape.
The lower jaw holds at least ten pairs of teeth, with a possible count of twelve.
The genus name combines Latin terms for 'narrow' and 'nostril' with the Greek word for 'wing'.
The species name uses Latin for 'long' and Greek for 'head'.
The preserved skull measures 192 mm in length, suggesting a total size of 201 mm if complete.
He Xinlu, Yang Daihuan, and Su Chunkang named the genus in 1983.
Researchers propose the front teeth created an intermeshed trap likely used to catch fish from the water surface.
He et al. (1983) placed Angustinaripterus within the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
This animal lived from the Bajocian to the Oxfordian, between 170.9 and 154.8 million years ago.
David Unwin considers Angustinaripterus to be a member of the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae rather than Scaphognathinae.
